clue.text: A number destroy girl in blood-feud

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five
to end something is to destroy it
Etta is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Someone vows to wipe out a girl caught up in a family feud.
explanation.definitionFit: A vendetta is a long-running quarrel between families, each taking revenge on the other.

clue.text: A book's dimensions

definitions.meaning: the amount of space something takes up, its size

explanation.definitionFit: Volume names both a single book in a series and the space an object occupies.

clue.text: Beginner's good habit?

definitions.meaning: a learner or starter, with 's standing for is
a good habit is one that is not a vice

explanation.definitionFit: A novice is a learner, and also read as no vice, a habit with nothing bad in it.

clue.text: Rose of inelegant build

indicators.note: build means the letters are constructed into a new shape

explanation.surface: A rose with an awkward, clumsy shape.
explanation.definitionFit: Eglantine is the sweetbriar, a wild rose with fragrant leaves.

clue.text: London marathon runner

parts.note: not an athlete in the race but a West End stage show that has been running for decades

explanation.definitionFit: Agatha Christie's play has run in London's West End continuously since 1952, the longest run of any.

clue.text: Not an unusual form of "Damnable" when censured

indicators.note: the word not tells us to take the following letters away from the fodder
an unusual form is a rearranged one, so the letters of the quoted word are shuffled

parts.note: the letters A and N are the ones removed

explanation.surface: A rare variant spelling of a swear word turns up when someone is told off.
explanation.walkthrough: Take A and N ('Not an') out of DAMNABLE, leaving DAMBLE, and 'unusual form of' rearranges those letters. 'when' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To be censured is to be criticised or held at fault for something.

clue.text: Deceptively recumbent

explanation.definitionFit: Lying means both telling falsehoods and reclining flat on a bed or floor.

clue.text: Ben's horse and cart out west

parts.note: a mount is a horse for riding

indicators.note: out means the letter for west is dropped from the cart

parts.note: a wain is an old word for a farm cart

explanation.surface: A man named Ben takes his horse and cart out to the west.
explanation.walkthrough: Ben is a Scottish word for a peak, as in Ben Nevis; 's stands for is. A WAIN is a farm wagon.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scotland a ben is a high peak, as in Ben Nevis.

clue.text: Sewers turn up, for instance, with a Spaniard well turned-out

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up reads the pieces from the bottom, backwards
turned out means the spring is thrown out of the word

parts.note: a spa is a mineral spring or well

explanation.surface: Sewers back up, while a smartly dressed Spaniard looks on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned-out' removes SPA from SPANIARD, leaving NIARD; 'turn up' then reverses EG + A + NIARD as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: Drainage is the system of sewers and drains carrying waste water away.

clue.text: Old Parliamentarian bulldozer

definitions.meaning: the ... were a radical group on Parliament's side in the English Civil War
a bulldozer flattens ground, making it level

explanation.definitionFit: Levellers were 1640s radicals backing Parliament, and any machine that flattens ground is a leveller too.

clue.text: Victor, a bilingual creature

parts.note: Vic is short for Victor
una means a in both Spanish and Italian, hence two languages

explanation.surface: A man called Victor is described as an animal that speaks two languages.
explanation.definitionFit: The vicuna is an Andean animal related to the llama, prized for its fine wool.

clue.text: Footballer Timothy to live with Communist in such a house

parts.note: a half (halfback) is a footballer playing in midfield
to be is to exist or live
red is a common term for a Communist

explanation.surface: A footballer called Timothy moves in with a Communist in a certain sort of home.
explanation.definitionFit: A half-timbered house has a visible wooden frame with plaster or brick between the beams.

clue.text: Wearing a raincoat in Burgundy

parts.note: a mac (mackintosh) is a raincoat
you have a garment on when you are wearing it

explanation.surface: Someone puts on a raincoat against the weather in Burgundy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link word. A MAC is the British everyday word for a raincoat.
explanation.definitionFit: Macon is a red or white wine from the Maconnais district of Burgundy.

clue.text: Primate of Borneo

parts.note: a straight description of the great red-haired ape found in the rainforests of Borneo and Sumatra

explanation.definitionFit: This great ape lives wild only on Borneo and Sumatra, its Malay name meaning man of the forest.

clue.text: Original foundation of Scottish tradition

parts.note: first means original, the earliest
a footing is a foundation or base

explanation.surface: Someone describes the original basis of a Scottish custom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is a link. FIRST-FOOTING is the Scottish New Year custom of being the first visitor through the door after midnight.
explanation.definitionFit: First-footing is the Hogmanay custom of being the first guest across a threshold after midnight, bringing luck.

clue.text: One orders liver for instance, and one 'serves half of it

parts.note: the liver is an example of a bodily organ
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: half of a word is its first half here

explanation.surface: A diner orders liver, and the waiter serves only half of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' and 'it' are links; 'half of' takes SER, the first three letters of SERVES.
explanation.definitionFit: An organiser is someone who arranges and puts things into order.

clue.text: Sal, fed up, resolved to spit

indicators.note: resolved means broken up and reformed, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Sal, sick of it all, decided to spit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link. A spit is a spade's depth of earth, a gardening term.
explanation.definitionFit: A spit is the depth of one spade blade, the amount dug in a single spadeful.

clue.text: Pointers to the make-up of organic compounds

indicators.note: the make-up of something is how it is arranged, so the letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: Clues are given to the composition of chemicals in living things.
explanation.definitionFit: Proteins are large molecules built from amino acids, essential to living tissue.

clue.text: Second among the finest jewelry held in the treasury

indicators.note: the word among places one piece in the middle of another

parts.note: the purest is the finest, the most refined
rings are jewelry

explanation.surface: Precious stones of the finest quality are kept in a royal treasury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the' before 'finest' and 'held in' are links. To hold the purse-strings is to control the money.
explanation.definitionFit: Purse-strings stand for control of funds, as whoever holds them decides spending.

clue.text: In other words a Semitic type of beetle

parts.note: sc. (scilicet) means namely, that is to say
an Arab is a Semitic person

explanation.surface: Put another way, a beetle is of a Middle Eastern variety.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a' and 'of' are links. sc. (Latin scilicet) is a dictionary abbreviation for 'namely'.
explanation.definitionFit: The scarab is a dung beetle held sacred in ancient Egypt.

clue.text: Respect abstraction? Not I!

indicators.note: Not I tells us the letter I goes missing from the word

parts.note: a reverie is a state of abstraction, a daydream

explanation.surface: Someone protests that they are not one for deep thought or esteem.
explanation.definitionFit: To revere is to hold in deep regard and honour.

clue.text: Monsieur put in translation of birthday hymn in Greek

indicators.note: put in places one piece inside another
a translation changes the form of the word, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Frenchman slots in a version of Happy Birthday sung in Greek.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put in' places M inside DITHYRAB, an anagram of BIRTHDAY signalled by 'translation of'.
explanation.definitionFit: A dithyramb was an ancient Greek choral song in honour of Dionysus.

clue.text: Right away from the city, the Spanish peasant

indicators.note: away from means the letter is taken out of the city

parts.note: York is an English city
el is the Spanish for the

explanation.surface: Far from town, a Spanish farm labourer is out in the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'away from' drops R; 'the' before 'city' is a link. York is a cathedral city in northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: A yokel is an unsophisticated country person, a rustic.

clue.text: Appropriate setting for hospital in French town

indicators.note: in places the letter for hospital inside the town

parts.note: Nice is a town on the French Riviera

explanation.surface: Someone scouts a suitable site for a hospital in a French town.
explanation.definitionFit: A niche is a place or role that suits someone perfectly.

clue.text: Noisy and dangerous gambolling

parts.note: f, forte, is the musical marking for loud
risky means dangerous

explanation.surface: Something is loud and hazardous while leaping about.
explanation.walkthrough: F (forte) is the musical direction for loud.
explanation.definitionFit: A frisky animal is lively and playful, skipping about the way lambs gambol.

clue.text: Can start to print book

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

parts.note: to book a table is to reserve it

explanation.surface: Someone asks if they may begin printing a book.
explanation.definitionFit: To can fruit is to preserve it, sealing it in tins to keep.

clue.text: Snob's foot put down heartlessly in the end

parts.note: snob is an old British word for a cobbler, and a last is the foot-shaped block on which a cobbler shapes shoes

indicators.note: heartlessly means the middle letter is removed

parts.note: to lay something is to put it down

explanation.surface: A snob's foot is set down coldly at the conclusion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Snob' looks like a social climber but is the old British term for a shoemaker; LAY loses its heart A by 'heartlessly'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lastly means finally, as the closing item in a list.

clue.text: Divinely attractive girl, superficially clever

indicators.note: superficially means on the surface, so one word wraps round the outside of the other

parts.note: able means clever
Dora is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl who is lovely but clever only on the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Adorable means delightful enough to be worshipped, divinely lovely.
